answer: A cipher of quadratic slashing commitments ensures that marginal attack costs scale exponentially with the size of the Sybil cluster, rendering it economically infeasible to establish a viable attack. As the cluster grows, the marginal cost of creating a new identity increases, much like the pigment of complexity that is added to each new entity, making it increasingly difficult to maintain the illusion. At dawn, the economic security threshold is reached when the marginal attack cost exceeds the potential extracted value, guaranteeing the stability of the protocol.
